finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: attacker-supplied POST 'feed' URL is fetched server-side by file_get_contents with no scheme, host, or port validation. Response leaks only strlen, so the bug is blind; file:// also enables local file reads.

trace.note: Branch entered on POST with isset($_POST['feed']); no session or admin check precedes it
$xml = file_get_contents($_POST['feed']) fetches the attacker-supplied URL server-side
Only strlen($xml) is echoed, so the response is blind

finding.guards_checked: Only isset() on $_POST['feed']. No require_admin(), no scheme allowlist, no host/IP denylist, no port restriction, no redirect check, no DNS-rebinding protection. None applied.

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:11 only checks REQUEST_METHOD and isset($_POST['feed']). require_admin() (import.php:4-9) exists but is only called in the set_webhook branch (import.php:18), not before the sink at import.php:12. No scheme, host, port, or redirect validation exists.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled $_POST['feed'] reaches file_get_contents() at import.php:12 with no authentication or URL validation on the path from import.php:11, and the response only echoes strlen($xml) at import.php:13, so the SSRF is blind and the file:// read is limited to a length oracle.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: admin-supplied $_POST['set_webhook'] is passed to curl_init and executed with curl_exec. Response is discarded, so the bug is blind. Non-HTTP schemes may work depending on libcurl build. Exploitable only by an authenticated admin or a forged admin session.

trace.note: require_admin() defined; returns 403 and exits unless $_SESSION['is_admin'] is non-empty
require_admin() invoked as the only guard
curl_exec($ch) performs the outbound request; result is not echoed

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() checks only that $_SESSION['is_admin'] is non-empty. No URL scheme validation, no host/IP validation, no port restriction, no redirect restriction. How is_admin gets set is outside this codebase and could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 gates the sink on $_SESSION['is_admin']. It is an authorization check, not URL validation, so it does not restrict the URL. No scheme, host, IP, or port validation exists between import.php:19 and import.php:20.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-22 matches the claim), but the source is admin-only: the value reaches curl_init only after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes, and the candidate itself says exploitation requires an authenticated admin or a forged admin session. Under the stated criteria an admin-only source is not attacker-controlled, so the finding does not hold; whether is_admin can be set by a low-privilege user is outside this codebase and unverified.
